neighbours.label: The setup of a correction to an assumed belief ('it's not necessarily...', 'the truth is...'), vs plain statements of requirement or cause
fire: Most diets fail, and it's not necessarily because people lack willpower.
Critics call the mayor reckless. The reality is far less dramatic than that.
Plenty of bands break up, but it isn't necessarily about money.
Everyone assumes the drug is safe. The truth is that nobody has tested it in children.
A degree helps, though it's not necessarily what employers care about most.
People blame the weather for the crash. The truth is the pilot was exhausted.
Small shops close often, and it's not necessarily a sign of a bad economy.
Many think the castle is medieval. The reality is it was built in 1890.
quiet: Most diets fail because people stop following them after a few weeks.
Critics call the mayor reckless and want a recall vote next spring.
Plenty of bands break up after their second album.
Everyone assumes the drug is safe because it was approved last year.
A degree is required for most positions at the agency.
People blame the weather for the crash on the icy highway.
Small shops close on Sundays in most of the town.
Many visitors think the castle is beautiful at sunset.

predictions: Correction setups reach 0.3-0.6; 'it is not necessary to' and plain causes stay under 0.2.
notes: Probe: 'The truth is more complex' 0.59, 'it's not necessarily due to' 0.53, 'Registration is not necessary if' 0.46; 'It is not necessary to bring towels' 0.055, 'the cause is usually' 0.19, 'is however required' 0.035. Hypothesis is loose.
